subject: Operational liability mapping for Private VPC — request for fallback attribution
messages:
From: Amelia Rogers <amelia@orion-analytics.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: Ben Turner <b.turner@orion-analytics.com>, contracts@orion-analytics.com
Date: 2028-07-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mapping responsibilities for Private VPC deployment

Hi Priyom,

We’re finalizing the architecture for our Private VPC deployment with Redwood and legal asked that we get an explicit mapping of operational responsibilities for availability and latency. Orion will manage the customer-owned edge routers, the peering, and the on-prem firewall cluster; Redwood will manage model serving inside the private deployment and the control plane that sits in our VPC.

Two asks:
- Can you provide a short matrix that shows which party owns which failure modes (e.g., peering outage, BGP flap, Redis KV cache miss on Redwood side, KMS rotation impact on model key access) and how those map to SLA credits or fallbacks?
- We also want a proposal for a fallback attribution policy: if tail latency crosses X% over SLO, who absorbs the credit and what evidence is required?

We have attached a network diagram and a draft procurement checklist.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call if that helps.

—Amelia
Orion Analytics

Attachments:
- orion_vpc_diagram.png (image)
- procurement-checklist.pdf (referenced)

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Rogers <amelia@orion-analytics.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mapping responsibilities for Private VPC deployment

Amelia — thanks for the detail and the diagram. I’ve sketched an initial responsibility matrix and attached it (sla-resp-matrix-draft.xlsx). High-level notes below, followed by a proposed evidence checklist and a suggested fallback attribution policy.

High-level mapping (summary):
- Redwood-owned: model-serving runtime, tokenization service, model weights storage (when pinned), KV cache, replica scheduling, and the control-plane components that coordinate model versioning.
- Customer-owned: physical network, peering, on-prem firewalls, edge load balancer, and external DNS.
- Shared: anything that crosses the VPC boundary (egress filters, NAT, cloud provider peering fabric) — we propose a "shared-resp" bucket with thresholds for when each side is considered primary.

Fallback attribution proposal (draft):
1) Measurement window: 5-minute rolling windows with p99/p999 latency buckets.
2) Attribution triggers: if p99 > SLO by >= 20% for > 10 consecutive minutes, run attribution.
3) Evidence: Redwood will produce server-side traces (request latency, kv cache hit rates, tail GC events), customer must produce network telemetry (flow logs, peering logs, router/syslog).
4) Arbitration: if logs point to packet loss/latency pre-ingress, customer responsibility; if requests reach our ingress and we show processing backlog, Redwood responsibility.

Action items I’m proposing:
- We’ll finalize the matrix into an SLA appendix we can attach to the Master Services Agreement.
- Engineering (Karthik) will draft an instrumentation checklist for both sides (what logs/metrics to preserve).
- Legal (Lauren) to draft contractual language for the shared-resp bucket and attribution arbitration clause.

Can you confirm Orion can provide the flow logs and peering metrics for any disputed windows? If yes, I’ll convert this to an appendix draft and share.

Thanks,
Priyom
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments:
- sla-resp-matrix-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Rogers <amelia@orion-analytics.com>, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-25T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mapping responsibilities for Private VPC deployment

Amelia — quick technical follow-up from the infra team. A few practical items we want to confirm before we finalize the appendix:

- Ingress termination: do you expect Redwood to terminate TLS at our ingress inside your VPC or will TLS be terminated at your edge LB? Termination point affects where we can insert request IDs for attribution.
- KV cache boundaries: we plan to keep local per-instance KV caches — if you have a shared cache upstream that influences request latency, we’ll mark that as customer-side.
- KMS: if customer-managed keys (CMK) are used for model weights decrypt, we need to define expected rotation windows and an out-of-band fallback for key unavailability.

We also recommend adding a small header that both sides propagate (X-ORION-TRACER or similar) so traces can be correlated during dispute windows. Happy to lay out the exact fields we expect.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Turner <b.turner@orion-analytics.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@orion-analytics.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-26T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mapping responsibilities for Private VPC deployment

Thanks for the quick draft. A couple of procurement/legal points from our side:

- Orion is ok with Redwood’s operational ownership of the runtime, but we need the contract to cap Redwood credits to incidents where the fault is demonstrably inside Redwood’s network/CIDR.
- For latency breaches that are "shared-resp", we propose a 60/40 apportionment for crediting during the first occurrence and a contingency to revisit after three occurrences in a rolling 90-day window.
- We will provide flow logs (as requested) but need clarity on retention windows; Orion can't retain packet-level logs for more than 30 days. If Redwood requires longer evidence, we need to discuss an evidence escrow arrangement.

Can Lauren propose contract language that:
1) Specifies the measurement windows and evidence needed,
2) Defines the apportionment approach for shared-resp,
3) Describes the evidence-escrow option (S3 bucket + access token exchange) if retention beyond 30 days is required.

Regards,
Ben Turner
Procurement, Orion Analytics

Attachments referenced:
- procurement_terms.docx (not attached in thread)

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Rogers <amelia@orion-analytics.com>, Ben Turner <b.turner@orion-analytics.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-26T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mapping responsibilities for Private VPC deployment

Folks — good thread, thank you. Summary and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary decisions: 
- Redwood owns model-serving runtime, control-plane components, and server-side instrumentation.
- Orion owns network fabric up to our ingress, peering, and on-prem firewalls.
- Shared-resp bucket will be used for cross-boundary incidents; initial apportionment proposed as 60/40 (customer/redwood) for first occurrence, reviewed after three incidents in 90 days.
- Evidence: Redwood will provide server-side traces and metrics for 90 days; Orion will provide flow logs for 30 days. If longer retention is required for arbitration, we’ll discuss an evidence-escrow S3 arrangement (Ben’s team to confirm retention/controls).

Deliverables and owners: 
- priyom_das: produce SLA appendix draft (attach redwood-private-sla-appendix-draft.pdf) by EOD Friday with the matrix and the fallback policy.
- karthik_iyer: produce instrumentation checklist and sample header format (X-ORION-TRACE-ID) by next Wed.
- lauren_bishop: draft contractual language for shared-resp apportionment and evidence-escrow options (target: next Fri).
- ben.turner@orion-analytics.com: confirm whether Orion can provide a 90-day aggregated retention of flow metrics (not packet capture) as a minimum.

If that aligns, I’ll create a short appendix and loop in Legal for the formal addendum. We should also schedule a 30-minute alignment call — I’ll send calendar invites after Ben confirms retention parameters.

Thanks — Priyom
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood-private-sla-appendix-draft.pdf (attachment stub)
